---
title: "Cross-sections & Ports"
sidebar: get-started
---

Choose an OrcaPen cross-section before routing, then use the actual ports
returned by the selected cell. A layout port describes a connection plane;
solver terminals and electrical reference conductors are separate choices.

## Select a cross-section

The active PDK registers CPW, coupled-CPW, strip, etch, launcher, and junction
sections. Named choices include `coplanar_waveguide`, `cpw_6_7_6`,
and `cpw_6_10_6`; inspect their definitions rather than inferring geometry
from a display name.

- [PDK registry and cross-section definitions](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/aee7f8b848895f2d107f6b086310e866e8381f73/orcapen_sc_pdk/pdk.py)
- [Technology functions](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/aee7f8b848895f2d107f6b086310e866e8381f73/orcapen_sc_pdk/tech.py)
- [Layers & Stack](layers.qmd)

Activate OrcaPen before resolving a named section. Use a matching section at
each connection, including trace width, gap, and layer choices.

## Read layout ports

Inspect each cell's actual port names, physical centre, orientation, width,
type, and layer. GDSFactory's physical-unit properties such as `dcenter`
and `dwidth` use micrometres; integer database coordinates use a different scale.

Forward or connect actual child ports using
[GDSFactory instances and ports](https://gdsfactory.github.io/gdsfactory/notebooks/01_references/).
The [OrcaPen cell gallery](../public-pdk-examples/index.md) and
[primitive descriptions](../public-pdk-examples/shared-primitives.md) identify
factory-specific connection and locator roles.

## Choose the electrical problem separately

A nonmetal locator can identify a sheet without creating metal or assigning
an excitation. For voltage, current, terminal ordering, or reference impedance,
use [S-parameters & Ports](../simulation/requirements/driven-terminal.qmd).
For a uniform-line model, use [Cross-section Simulation](../simulation/requirements/q2d-cross-section.qmd).
